item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":1,"rationale":"The President immediately assigns an internal coordinating role to the APHS/CT; this is an executive-organization designation, not a change to legal rights.","evidence":"is hereby designated as the National Continuity Coordinator"},{"segment_id":"2","code":1,"rationale":"The Coordinator and CPCC are directed to coordinate policy development and implementation on an ongoing basis, without directive authority; the consequence is internal executive management.","evidence":"shall coordinate the development and implementation of continuity policy"},{"segment_id":"3","code":1,"rationale":"The directive presently categorizes agencies for internal continuity planning according to their governmental roles; this is administrative organization rather than a substantive legal consequence.","evidence":"each executive department and agency is assigned to a category"},{"segment_id":"4","code":1,"rationale":"The Secretary and Coordinator must coordinate operations, develop a plan, and submit it for later presidential approval; these are internal assignments, planning, and reporting duties.","evidence":"The Plan shall be submitted to the President for approval"},{"segment_id":"5","code":1,"rationale":"Executive officials and programs must coordinate and integrate continuity planning with other branches and nonfederal entities; this is operational coordination rather than a dictated legal outcome.","evidence":"shall be appropriately coordinated with those of the legislative and judicial branches"},{"segment_id":"6","code":1,"rationale":"The Secretary and agencies must coordinate and maintain specified internal continuity capabilities, while the President retains authority to set the later COGCON level; these are operational-readiness requirements.","evidence":"Executive departments and agencies shall comply with the requirements and assigned responsibilities under the COGCON program"},{"segment_id":"7","code":2,"rationale":"Among the assigned administrative duties, the Secretary is specifically required to make grant funding available later to designated recipients, producing a prescribed funding consequence through agency administration.","evidence":"Make available continuity planning and exercise funding, in the form of grants as provided by law"},{"segment_id":"8","code":1,"rationale":"Defense and agency heads must provide communications, activate plans, appoint coordinators, plan, budget, test, and train; these are internal continuity operations and management duties.","evidence":"Heads of executive departments and agencies shall execute their respective department or agency COOP plans"},{"segment_id":"9","code":1,"rationale":"Executive implementers must administer the directive consistently with succession law and consult relevant officials; this is an implementation constraint rather than an independent legal consequence.","evidence":"This directive shall be implemented in a manner that is consistent with"},{"segment_id":"10","code":1,"rationale":"Agency heads must maintain internal support for officials involved in presidential succession so they remain prepared to implement existing law.","evidence":"shall ensure that appropriate support is available"},{"segment_id":"11","code":1,"rationale":"The President immediately revokes a prior internal continuity directive, incorporates annexes, and prescribes information-handling rules; these are executive housekeeping and administrative-security measures.","evidence":"Presidential Decision Directive-67 of October 21, 1998 (\"Enduring Constitutional Government and Continuity of Government Operations\"), including all Annexes thereto, is hereby revoked."}]}
